findings.message: The previous finding asked that totals stay unchanged when the PR or build answer is junk. The old test asserted `.totals.hosted_s == 0`. The new p/b loop asserts only row fields and `note`, and no totals at all. Add a totals assertion to the loop. For the PR cases, `.totals.prs_open == 0` and `.totals.jobs == 2`. For the build cases, `.totals.hosted_s == 0`.
findings.scenario: The PR endpoint returns `[]`. If an unread PR were counted in `totals.prs_open`, or the row dropped out of `totals.jobs`, the loop would still pass because it only checks `rows[0]`.

findings.message: The new guard checks only that `.items` is an array. If the elements are not objects, the next `jq` (`sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp)`) errors, `name` comes back empty, and `status_job` prints `{job:"-",phase:"-"}`. That reads 'could not parse the cluster answer' as 'no Job exists'. Make the guard `.items | type == "array" and all(type == "object")`, or fail to the `?` answer when the name extraction fails.
findings.scenario: kubectl answers `{"items":[1]}`. The guard passes, the name `jq` errors silently, and the row gets phase `-` with no `unread: cluster` note, so it looks like a change with no Job.
